title: Coherent mapping spaces as twisted-arrow ends and Fubini
statement:
Use universes, quasicategories, coherent functors and mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the space category $\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}$ of [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces], coherent Hom bifunctors of [lem-coef-infinity-hom-bifunctor-functoriality], and the construction $\operatorname{Tw}$ with projection $(s,t)$ of [lem-coef-twisted-arrow-left-fibration]. Let $C,D$ be $\mathcal V$-small quasicategories, and let $\mathcal E$ be a quasicategory in a containing universe with $\mathcal V$-small mapping spaces. For coherent $F,G:C\to\mathcal E$ there is an equivalence of whole mapping spaces
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(C,\mathcal E)}(F,G)\simeq\lim_{(c\to c')\in\operatorname{Tw}(C)}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(F(c),G(c')).$$
The limit is the coherent limit in $\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}$ of the displayed diagram composed with $(s,t)$, in the sense of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. The projection at the identity arrow of $c$ is the component-evaluation map. For $F,G:C\times D\to\mathcal E$, product decomposition of twisted arrows and Fubini give
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(C\times D,\mathcal E)}(F,G)\simeq\lim_{(d\to d')\in\operatorname{Tw}(D)}\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(C,\mathcal E)}(F(-,d),G(-,d')).$$
Here the inner mapping space is the $\operatorname{Tw}(C)$-limit of $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(F(c,d),G(c',d'))$, and either order of the two limits gives the same space. These small limits exist, admit $\mathcal V$-small Kan models, and taking them carries coherent natural equivalences of the indexed diagrams to equivalences, including their inverse homotopies. All identifications commute with component evaluation, restriction, and additional simplicial parameters, naturally in $F,G$. Empty $C$ or $D$ is allowed.

source.place: Kerodon Example 8.3.4.22 (03P7), mapping spaces as limits over twisted arrows, read online 2026-10-17. The product formula is the agent-formulated Fubini consequence using the degreewise identity Tw(C x D) = Tw(C) x Tw(D). Archival copy WANTED; Kerodon identifier, not a Stacks Project tag.
